title: Closed support kernel and internal sheaf adjunction over an arbitrary ring
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves $A_T$ on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use inverse and direct images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Put $i^!_0F=i^*\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$, with the restriction adjunction unit as arrow. Then $i_*$ is exact and left adjoint to $i^!_0$, and $i^!_0$ takes injective $A_X$-module sheaves to injective $A_Z$-module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every $A_Z$-module sheaf $G$ and $A_X$-module sheaf $F$ there is a natural isomorphism of $A_X$-module sheaves
$$\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(i_*G,F)\cong i_*\mathcal Hom_{A_Z}(G,i^!_0F).$$
Here sheaf Hom means the sheaf of module maps after restriction to each slice site [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The isomorphism on each etale object $V\to X$ is the support adjunction for $Z\times_XV\hookrightarrow V$, identifying supported sections by the same kernel of restriction to $U\times_XV$. Its inverse is induced by the support inclusion $i_*i^!_0F\to F$. These identifications commute with further etale restriction, with maps of $F,G$, and with their $A$-actions. No finiteness condition is imposed on $A$ or on the sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), its support adjunction, localized over each etale object; module-linear internal form of the construction in Section 09XP. ILO Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 7.6.10, p. 313 uses its derived form.

proof.text: Write $P(F)=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$, $a_F:P(F)\to F$ and $H(F)=i^*P(F)$. The faithful exact forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] computes this kernel on underlying abelian sheaves. The constant-coefficient inverse images, units and counits have those same underlying abelian maps by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and direct image does too by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Consequently [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] supplies an underlying isomorphism $q_F:P(F)\to i_*H(F)$, specifically the closed unit on $P(F)$. That unit is a module morphism by the module adjunction just cited, so its inverse is also module-linear. Thus $c_F=a_Fq_F^{-1}:i_*H(F)\to F$ is a natural module-linear support inclusion. Exactness of abelian $i_*$ from the support lemma implies exactness on module sheaves: forgetting scalars preserves kernels and cokernels and reflects zero objects, so it reflects exactness. The kernel construction on morphisms is the unique factorization of $P(F)\to F\to F'$ through $P(F')$, and hence gives the functor $H$.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), proof and preceding supported-sheaf definition; module exactness is Tag 03DA (sites-modules-lemma-abelian).

proof.text:
Let $T_{G,F}$ be the abelian support-adjunction bijection of [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction]. Concretely, $T_{G,F}$ is computed as follows. The open immersion $j$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] the sections of $j^*i_*G$ over $W\to U$ are $G(W\times_XZ)=G(\varnothing)=0$ (the empty covering of the empty scheme); hence $j^*i_*G=0$, and by naturality of the unit every $h:i_*G\to F$ is killed by $F\to j_*j^*F$ and factors uniquely as $h=a_Fh'$. Put $T_{G,F}(h)=k$, the unique map with $i_*k=q_Fh'$ [lem-kun-04ca]. Its inverse is $k\mapsto c_F i_*k$: indeed $c_Fi_*T_{G,F}(h)=a_Fq_F^{-1}q_Fh'=h$, and $c_Fi_*k=a_F(q_F^{-1}i_*k)$ has $h'=q_F^{-1}i_*k$, so $T_{G,F}(c_Fi_*k)=k$; naturality in $G$ and $F$ follows from naturality of $a$ and $q$. For $a\in A$, naturality of this additive bijection gives
$$T_{G,F}(h\,i_*\mu_a^G)=T_{G,F}(h)\mu_a^G,\qquad T_{G,F}(\mu_a^F h)=H(\mu_a^F)T_{G,F}(h).$$
Here $H(\mu_a^F)=\mu_a^{H(F)}$ by the kernel and inverse-image module structures of Step 1. Hence $h$ commutes with multiplication by every $a$ if and only if its transpose does. For a constant ring sheaf this is precisely module-linearity: a section of $A_T$ is locally represented by an element of $A$, by its sheafification definition [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the required equality is local. Thus $T$ restricts to natural bijections on module morphisms. These are additive and $A$-linear, with the same inverse $k\mapsto c_F i_*k$. This proves $i_*\dashv H=i^!_0$ over $A$. The identical scalar argument lifts full faithfulness in [lem-kun-04ca] to module sheaves: the abelian preimage of a module map commutes with every $\mu_a$ by faithfulness.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, displayed Hom identity and its support-factorization proof; scalar-equivariant restriction of that bijection.

proof.text: Let $I$ be injective in $\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$ and $M\hookrightarrow N$ a monomorphism in $\operatorname{Mod}(A_Z)$. Step 1 makes $i_*M\to i_*N$ a monomorphism. Transpose a given module map $M\to H(I)$ by Step 2 to $i_*M\to I$. Injectivity extends it to $i_*N\to I$. Transposing back gives $N\to H(I)$ extending the original map, by naturality of the bijection with respect to $M\to N$. This is exactly the injectivity criterion of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No assertion about injectivity after forgetting scalars is used.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, final sentence of the proof, expanded by the injective-object extension criterion.

proof.text:
Fix an etale object $V\to X$ and put $Z_V=Z\times_XV$, $U_V=U\times_XV$. The immersion $i_V:Z_V\to V$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; its complement is the inverse image of the open set $U$, namely $U_V$. The etale sites of $V,Z_V,U_V$ identify with the corresponding slice sites: $Z_V\to Z$ and $U_V\to U$ are etale as base changes of $V\to X$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; for $T\to S$ etale, a scheme $W\to T$ is etale over $T$ if and only if $W\to T\to S$ is etale over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so the objects agree, and coverings are the same jointly surjective families. Likewise $W\times_XZ=W\times_VZ_V$ is an etale $Z_V$-scheme for $W\to V$ etale. Use restriction as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies abelian etale inverse image with this sectionwise restriction, including the unit. Applied to scalar multiplications, its naturality makes this identification module-linear for constant coefficients. The module inverse-image identification of the rings is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For $W\to V$, the direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives
$$(i_*G)|_V(W)=G(W\times_XZ)=i_{V*}(G|_{Z_V})(W).$$
The same formula for $j_*$ and its restriction unit gives
$$P(F)|_V(W)=\ker\bigl(F(W)\to F(W\times_XU)\bigr)=P_V(F|_V)(W).$$
These are equalities on sections and arrows, so include the kernel inclusions and all scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support), sectionwise supported-subsheaf formula; Tag 01QR (morphisms-lemma-base-change-closed-immersion); etale restriction of direct image and its unit.

proof.text:
Apply the construction of Step 1 on $V$. Write $H_V=i_V^*P_V$ and $q_{V,F|_V}:P_V(F|_V)\to i_{V*}H_V(F|_V)$. Restricting $q_F$ to $V$ instead gives, by Step 4, an isomorphism $r_V:P_V(F|_V)\to i_{V*}(H(F)|_{Z_V})$. Full faithfulness of $i_{V*}$ [lem-kun-04ca], lifted to module morphisms as in Step 2, therefore gives a unique module isomorphism
$$b_V:H(F)|_{Z_V}\longrightarrow H_V(F|_V),\qquad i_{V*}b_V=q_{V,F|_V}r_V^{-1}.$$
Its defining equality implies
$$c_{V,F|_V}\,i_{V*}b_V=c_F|_V.$$
In particular $b_V$ is normalized by the actual support inclusion, rather than an unspecified identification. No inverse-image base-change theorem is required for this comparison.

source.place: Tags 04CA (proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward) and 09XQ: compare the two supported-sheaf presentations using full faithfulness.

proof.text:
By [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and Step 4, a section over $V$ of the left side of the desired isomorphism is a module map $h:i_{V*}(G|_{Z_V})\to F|_V$. Step 2 applied on $V$ sends it bijectively to $T_V(h):G|_{Z_V}\to H_V(F|_V)$. Define
$$\Phi_V(h)=b_V^{-1}T_V(h)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{Z_V}}(G|_{Z_V},H(F)|_{Z_V}).$$
The latter group is exactly $(i_*\mathcal Hom_{A_Z}(G,H(F)))(V)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Its inverse sends $k$ to $(c_F|_V)i_{V*}k$, by the normalization in Step 5. Substituting the two formulas and the two inverse adjunction identities verifies both composites are the identity. Thus each $\Phi_V$ is a bijection with precisely the support-inclusion-induced inverse required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, support adjunction on the etale scheme V; the slice definition of internal sheaf Hom.

proof.text: For an arrow $W\to V$ of etale objects, restrict the formula $h=(c_F|_V)i_{V*}\Phi_V(h)$ to $W$. The sectionwise identifications of Step 4 give $h|_W=(c_F|_W)i_{W*}(\Phi_V(h)|_{Z_W})$. Uniqueness in the bijection of Step 6 then gives $\Phi_W(h|_W)=\Phi_V(h)|_{Z_W}$. This proves compatibility with all sheaf restriction maps [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For maps $G'\to G$ and $F\to F'$, the same inverse formula, using naturality of $c$, proves naturality by precomposition and postcomposition. Finally $c_F|_V$ and $i_{V*}$ are $A_V$-linear, so the inverse satisfies $\Psi_V(a k)=a\Psi_V(k)$ for every $a\in A_X(V)$ (acting on the right through restriction to $Z_V$). Its inverse $\Phi_V$ is therefore also $A_X(V)$-linear. Hence these bijections are the claimed natural isomorphism of module sheaves. All steps allowed arbitrary $A,F,G$; none used a finite generation or finiteness hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem etale_closed_sheaf_internal_adjunction {Z U X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) : PreservesFiniteLimits (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i) ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i) ∧ ∃ a : lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i ⊣ kernel (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).unit ⋙ upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i, (∀ F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).unit.app ((kernel (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).unit).obj F) ≫ a.counit.app F = (kernel.ι (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).unit).app F) ∧ (∀ I : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), Injective I → Injective ((kernel (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).unit ⋙ upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj I)) ∧ ∃ e : etaleClosedSheafHomSource A i ≅ etaleClosedSheafHomTarget A i j, ∀ (G : Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)), e.inv.app (op G, F) = etaleClosedSheafHomComparison A i j a G F
lean.note: Ordinary internal Hom is the existing tensor-Hom object on ModuleCat-valued etale sheaves, equivalently maps on slice sites. The natural isomorphism is normalized by its inverse: lax direct-image tensor map, pushed-forward evaluation, and the support counit. The latter is fixed by the closed unit/kernel-inclusion equation. No derived Hom or arbitrary comparison map is substituted. The kernel functor is written inline to avoid duplicating the support definitions published in the downstream localization module or importing that consumer.
